Salutation to Śiva and Śivā.
The Hymn to the Greatness of the Supreme Śambhu.
First Chapter.
May the all-pervasive Śrī Parameśvara, the auspicious Śiva who is pure consciousness, protect us— he whose body is the wave of light arising from the collision of manifold powers.

O Śrī Śambhu, even the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs, along with the scriptures, the philosophical systems, the sciences with their branches, and minds endowed with great vigilance, do not see the limit of Your majesty when set upon the path of praise. How then could they describe You— the infinite Supreme Śiva, the Guru— who are without beginning or end?
Therefore, following my own wisdom, I too shall praise a small portion of your life story.
Where is the manifestation of your blissful self, that ocean of supreme, boundless nectar?
And where are the poet-bees—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the others—who are submerged in the fragrance of devotion to you?
O Śrī Śambhu, does this expansion of delusion not produce in them a supreme sense of their own true nature? Why is this so?
Just as that was wonderful, so too it is no fault that you are praised by me according to the power of my own intellect. || 2 ||

O Paraśiva, O Śambhu whose nature is self-luminous, you alone are beyond all things, shining forth completely through auspicious visible manifestations— those various objects of diverse forms that have arisen from the expansion of the Self as "I am I" and "this is I," and which possess infinite glory.
"There is no other superior to you; thus, O Guru, I recognize you here by your very nature. (3)

This very self of one's own is filled with the supreme Brahman, which is consciousness, bliss, and existence; yet it is humbled by the states of transmigratory existence, which are exceedingly difficult to overcome and consist of the assumed play of māyā.

O Supreme Person, because you are the self of all, the truth of your auspicious majesty, O Śrī Guru, is reached as non-dual through your words of truth, which transcend the distinctions of conceptual limitations. 4.

Having obtained the Śāmbhavī initiation— ordained by a Guru who is Śiva himself, proclaimed in the scriptures of the divine seed-syllables, skilled in bestowing identity with the venerable Śambhu, and the destroyer of birth and death—
one becomes full through the yoga of meditating on the feet of Paraśiva, having pierced through the state of bondage (paśutva) which is to be pierced.
The wise one attains that Brahman, the supreme state known through the knowledge of the auspicious Aghora-Brahma-mantra. || 5 ||
Having realized that this physical body is like the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), being neither identical to nor different from its father,
and having been liberated from ignorance through the words of the Śiva-guru, one becomes tranquil through self-knowledge;
with a mind intent on worshipping the feet of Paraśiva, the Lord who is the sole Self of all, [one attains liberation].
O Great Death of Death! That certain one who is a yogi conquers birth and death.
If you realize, through the words of the Guru Śiva, that within this body— a city of nine gates, composed of the five elements and the sense organs, whether male, female, or neuter—
you are none other than the mass of the innermost sheath of incomparable bliss, which is the pure consciousness beyond the impurity of the mind and its perceptions; [then you are liberated].
O Supreme Śiva, you whose form is divided into six aspects—you are that wise one who attains the state of being the universal form.

O Lord of All, Sovereign of Śrīpura! If the entire manifold of the visible universe were known in its true nature by the Guru who is Śiva himself, then those powers of yours— beginning with Ananta and others, beginning with Śrīparā and others, possessing boundless majesty, extending from Mātṛkā to Kṣakāra, and manifesting as the dwellings of the three worlds— would be fully realized.
When they cause those [objects] merged in the light of their own self to dissolve, those wise ones become yogins; that itself is liberation.
O Lord Śambhu, that very Śrī Parā, whose glory is manifested in sixfold and fivefold ways,
is praised by the Vedas as Śrī Sundarī when she is seated upon the throne of the King of Wheels.
Pervading the Yoginīs who manifest in countless millions everywhere,
and firmly established within Your splendor, she fashions the times of the beginning, middle, and end of the worlds.

O Supreme Śiva, whose form transcends space and time, you are that Power (Śakti) who, as Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī, has swallowed the ocean of the three worlds with the fire of universal destruction— the fire manifested by the splendor of your own nature through the surging waves of the fivefold flow; [you are she who removes] the ignorance of the great ones who possess devotion.
Through the gift of wisdom, you strike down death for the learned; that greatness is yours alone. 10.

O Śiva, if you are known here through the words of the Teacher by means of these six limbs—being omniscient, eternally satisfied, pervading the existent, the non-existent, and both, possessing beginningless awakening, independent, possessing an eternal and unimpaired self-power, of incomparable conduct, and infinite—and if you are perceived as the manifestation of the six powers; [The rest of the verse follows: ...then, O Lord, may my devotion to you be firm and constant, like that of the six-faced one (Kārttikeya) toward the six-faced Lord (Śiva). May I never be separated from you, who are the supreme goal, the source of all, the one whose nature is the sixfold path, and who are the very essence of the sixfold reality. May I always be intent upon your service, devoted to your feet, and free from all other desires. May I never turn away from you, the embodiment of the sixfold power, the one who dwells within the sixfold body, and the one who is the ultimate refuge for those seeking liberation. May I always be established in your grace, O Śiva, the one who is the sixfold light and the source of the sixfold world. May I never forget you, the one who is the sixfold consciousness and the master of the sixfold senses. May I always be absorbed in your meditation, O Śiva, the one who is the sixfold bliss and the destroyer of the sixfold afflictions. May I never be separated from you, the one who is the sixfold truth and the protector of the sixfold beings. That differentiation of yours, the Supreme Goddess, by which all your playful manifestations have been displayed within your own self since beginningless time. || 11 ||

Gāyatrī, the sustainer of the Vedas, the bestower of the fruit of a hundred sacrifices, and the one knowable through the Vedas and all scriptures— O Supreme Śiva, Your glorious Parā, the power of consciousness and the knowledge of Brahman, explains [all things]: She who is expressed as identical with the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman), who is the essence of all philosophical systems, whose true nature is manifest, and yet who is ultimately inexpressible.
The manifestation of the seven streams, the state of being composed of the three worlds, and all the fourfold [states] in their true essence.

Having realized that supreme primordial power— which is non-different from one's own self and is expert in navigating the vessel of the insubstantial nature of saṃsāra— one stands with the ego-sense unclouded by the notions of "body" or "consent," [perceiving] the three worlds as the pervasive expansion of the Brahman-universe, filled with one's own boundless self-luminosity.
Having known this, O Maheśa, that yogi becomes liberated and freed from worldly existence through your grace. 13.
O Lord of All, the truth here is that nothing exists other than the expansion of Your own self-luminous nature;
this very web of the sacred oral tradition from the mouth of Your supreme Guru is the form of Mīmāṃsā.

If you say that, setting aside one's own direct perception, the truth exists elsewhere as something devoid of sound, then those wise ones who would speculate thus will themselves undergo births and deaths through the burden of their limbs. 14.

Neither Brahmā, Viṣṇu, nor Rudra; neither the lords of the gods nor the immortals, nor the asuras; neither earth, nor water, nor fire, nor air, nor the expanse of the sky, nor the directions, nor time;
neither the Vedas, nor sacrifices, nor the sun and moon; neither the void, nor conceptual construction.
O You whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss, may Your own light—the one true state—be victorious! 15.

O Śambhu, those followers of the Siddhānta who, with their own intellectual prowess, possess no small pride, and who examine you through the means of valid cognition (pramāṇas) surrounded by the Śuddhavidyās that generate many opinions—
how can they, competing with one another here, attain the reality of your own splendor?
It transcends all, is free from the grasp of conceptual construction, unborn, and inaccessible to means of knowledge, logic, and the like. || 16 ||

O Supreme Śiva, some steadfast great souls, devoted to the words of their gurus, having abandoned worldly attachments, their intellects matured through fearless and profound wisdom, and liberated from all conceptual constructions—
such practitioners of yours, O Blessed One, become the targets of Your compassionate gaze, rendered free from both merit and sin.
Devoid of both what is to be done and what is not to be done, they behold you, the universal sovereign of the supreme state.

O Lord Śrīvibhu, this Siddhānta of Śambhu—expounded through the syllables of the Aghora-vidyā according to the words of the Guru Śiva—is here brought to completion under the guise of a hymn; thus, my impertinence is before you.
May whatever errors have arisen from deficiency or excess in this work be forgiven repeatedly by you, out of regard for me as your servant.
Abiding within my mind, please teach me the supreme object of knowledge: the collection of letters of the Mātṛkā.
Thus ends the first chapter, the Introduction, in the *Śrī-Dūrvāsakṛta-Paraśambhu-Mahimnastava*.
Chapter Two:
[The Praise of] the Glorious Radiance of Rays, the Self-Luminous Lamp that reveals the abodes of the three worlds.

O Maheśa, who is capable of describing through etymological analysis that [Reality] upon which even the intellect of the learned, beginning with Brahmā—when its steady wisdom has attained correct discernment—is destroyed by fear along with the Śruti? By whom, even one of expansive mind, can that be described? || 1 ||

O Supreme Śiva, the powers beginning with Parā and ending with Mātṛkā are yours, residing in the seats of earth, water, fire, touch, ether, and mind— these being the six lineages. Through your own six limbs, which possess the majesty of Brahmā and the others seated upon the lion-throne of the corpse, [you pervade all].
The thirty-two principal rays shine forth, having pervaded the entire universe with their own beams of light. || 2 ||

In that fourth state, where the path is revealed by the right inquiry of the intellect and the activity of speech is purposeful, and wherein the reality of the great sentence is not newly fashioned—therein occurs destruction.
Is that light or darkness? Does it belong to existence, non-existence, or both? Is it formless or indeed possessed of form?
O Lord, since destruction is not the definitive conclusion of either thought or speech, you are therefore beyond them both.

Knowledge, yoga, illumination, ritual injunction, dualistic cognition, the body, the intellect, the vital breath, the void, the ego, and excessive desire—these dwell within, taking refuge in their respective objects which are ultimately harmful.
Thus, this nature of the self as space has been thoroughly known by you; this is the true object of knowledge.
O Lord, You shine like butter hidden within milk, or like oil within a heap of sesame seeds.

If that wish-fulfilling tree of yours, whose fragrance is the cluster of blossoms consisting of the thirty-six principles, has been awakened by the words of the Śiva-guru and is experienced by you in its entirety, [then all is attained].

If it is argued that this very Pārijāta tree produces in the wise the realization of non-dual Brahman—that within the phenomenal world of selves, beginning from ourselves and ending with Brahmā, there is no other—it shines forth thus. || 5 ||
Even though reality is directly perceptible to him like a fruit in the palm of his hand, he does not know its true nature,
being overwhelmed by the darkness of ignorance produced by the prattle of various nets of philosophical tenets,
and by merits and demerits acquired through his own beginningless actions.
O Lord, you have been made to exist by Great Māyā through the notion of what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted.

If this one [Self] is distinct due to the various characteristics residing in all bodies and the manifold objects of the senses, and is bound by its own nature through the processes of birth and death— how can it be that it possesses divinity, humanity, the state of a serpent, and the nature of the soul of all living beings within a single body?
O you who possess the form of the illustrious Mahādeva, you remember [the goal] like an actor, yet you do not remember your own station. || 7 ||
Thus ends the second chapter, on the Rays of the Neck of the Supreme Power, in the *Śrī-Dūrvāsakṛta-Paraśambhu-Mahimnastava*. || 2 ||
The third chapter:
Being, consciousness, and greatness belong to your supreme Guru, the transcendent power of the Self.

Having condensed by nature the fire that exists at the end of time— the false lover during the first union— you, whose will is unimpeded, having become the abode of the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the world, proceed as far as the ocean of waters; thus manifesting yourself, you are victorious here, O manifestation of Viṣṇu’s Māyā.

Abiding within Māyā, your [power], whose essence is the flower-arrowed god [Kāma], at its own time— its majesty manifested through the knower, the object of knowledge, and the means of knowledge— having first produced Viriñci by the expansion of its own sprouts, subsequently pervades the state of the worlds through itself.
He tells you his name is Svayambhū, the Seed-form, because he is the creator of the universe's very soul.

Having attained a state of being subject to the qualities of His own unsurpassed will, He pervades the emanation of letters from *a* to *kṣa*, which is the ground for the manifestation of the dwellings of the three worlds; it possesses the various movements of the series of His own principles (*tattvas*) beginning with Śiva and ending with Earth, and extends to the realm of Brahmā’s egg.
O Śrīśambhu, you are the creator of the universe, your own self having been obscured by the triad of impurities.

The four ages (yugas) in the principle of Time (kālatattva) are your [emanations], and they are the sons of Dhātu; these twelve have been explained as the established knowers of the maintenance [of the world], along with their incarnations and wives.
And the Lords beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha, who uphold the ordinances of the ages, arise from your Necessity (niyati) and terminate within it.
Therefore, you are known as the abiding state of pure consciousness, radiant as a thousand suns.
(p. 8) Here,

[the sun] draws forth its own beginningless rays, which have as their objects the various false conceptual constructions arising from the delusions caused by the manifold nets of tenets produced in this cycle of existence, and which are distinguished by merit, demerit, and so forth.

Victorious is that non-contradiction with Your Self, which instantly awakens one— through the words of the Teacher— to the realization of one's own nature within the uniquely self-luminous fire of the utterly pure body, which is otherwise difficult to comprehend.

On the path to liberation, which is obscured by the qualities of one's own *māyā*— manifesting as the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, and appearing as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva in the forms of knowledge, will, and anger— certain wise travelers, illuminated by the fire of the scriptures and the wisdom arising from the words of the auspicious Guru, [proceed].
O Primordial Form, they approach you, who have been fashioned solely for protection through your compassion.

You are the first, the illusory Kāmadeva; therefore, you are the Creator (Vidhātṛ) in your own creation, Viṣṇu in its protection, and at the end, the form of the most powerful Mahārudra within your own manifestation.
You are Satya, Ananta, the Knower (Pramātṛ), and Śivaguru—by means of the powers of these forms of your own Self.
O All-pervading One, although You are richly endowed with qualities that are subject to Your own will, You are praised in reality as being "without qualities. Thus are You lauded.
By that power of will (*icchā-śakti*) through which this entire web of the world was swallowed up—
by means of its functions of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, and by its own course resembling a torrent of rain upon a lake—
that very power, through its infinite internal expansion, assumes the states of manifold and diverse volitions (*saṃkalpa*).
Having become manifest, you alone are the ocean of consciousness for the purpose of revealing your own limbs. || 8 ||
Thus ends the third section, on the rays of the trunk of the power of will (*icchāśakti*), in the *Paraśambhumahimnastava* composed by the venerable Dūrvāsas. || 3 ||
The fourth chapter:
the network of reality to be known, which reaches from the earth of Paraśiva down to its foundation;
variegated with the infinite expansion of karma, possessing incomparable majesty, and without beginning, middle, or end.

The ocean of the nectar of Brahman-bliss, expanded by the moon of the state of equal flavor (*samarasa*), manifests as the cause of the radiance of one's own Self; it reveals your great power of knowledge, O Flame of Awakening. || 1 ||

Just as the milk from a cow is one, so too is the manifestation of its own various qualities and sensory objects a single entity; yet, due to the diversity of tastes in describing it, there is a perceived multiplicity in that which is essentially one.
Like fire enveloped by the appearance of smoke in the sky, [the Self] is surrounded by the cognition of appearances such as blue and the like.
O Supreme Śiva, you are therefore intensely radiant and consist of the essence of true reality. || 2 ||
O Immaculate All-pervading One, from Your eternally undivided radiance, Māyā is sometimes produced; she whose nature is the power manifested through the various aspects of the three *guṇas*,
and who is characterized by the notion of duality through doctrines that employ diverse measures of valid cognition and are fraught with suffering.
The Vedic science, having extended the state of transmigratory existence, confirms the reality of your being. || 3 ||

Or rather, there is another aspect here: that which is called "Truth" (Satya), wherein the infinite power of pure manifestation shines forth; yet even that, whose essence is that [Truth], dissolves into the abyss of the Void.
And that nature of yours, which is Truth itself, is the Māyā of the one whose form is desire, through its own splendors.
Having brought forth this manifold expansion, You bring it into being; O You whose source is Your own Self, You pervade all this.

If, due to the identity of the powers of consciousness (*cit-śakti*), there were this state of duality consisting of "this" and "I"— namely, the dualistic cognition of the individual soul (*jīva*) and Brahman, and so forth, as well as that of the sun and the moon, and the mundane egg (*aṇḍa*) and the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*).

When the emergence of equilibrium occurs between the two winds known as prāṇa and apāna, which are like merit and demerit, then you become the supreme and foremost Lord Ānandanātha, who is both being and non-being. || 5 ||
This power of consciousness, shown to you by your auspicious Guru, is eternally pure; it leads the wise to the non-dual reality of Brahman, which is full of being, consciousness, and bliss.

If it is asked how there can be diverse paths in this world through the distinctions of the object of knowledge, the knower, and the act of knowing—[the answer is that these are merely for those who seek such distinctions].
O Supreme Lord, those established in ego manifest various forms of mudrās with joy.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, on the Rays of the Branch of Knowledge-Power, in the *Śrī-Dūrvāsakṛta-Paraśambhu-Mahimnastava*.
The Fifth Chapter:

The Ocean of Milk of Awakening to the Enjoyment of Relishing Each Respective Object of the Cognitive and Perceptual Faculties, [purified] by the rays of the rising moon of desire and by those washed from the mouth of speech.

If you, whose nature is action, have emerged from Śiva, you scatter the drops of the universe—which are bursting forth from the vast flood of your own vital breath—as the many paths of the expansion of meaning move and shift. || 1 ||
Whose path is unimpeded by the play of creation, maintenance, and dissolution; whose effort and whose renowned valor are all-encompassing; whose intellect has attained full maturity;
and whose power is abundant, extending beyond the count of the multitude of cosmic eggs and the vessels containing the Rudras—[to Him I bow].
The abode which is the existence of Brahman—that victory of yours, whose nature as the universal self takes the form of the mind. || 2 ||

O Hero, that which brings about repose in the distant realm, the totality of ritual action, and one's own essential reality— even without the movement of the external senses— by means of the inner light of the mind; that is the dissolution of independent nature, free from the logic of limiting adjuncts.
O Vimalaśiva, you are then the self that is the substratum of the senses, for the purpose of perceiving what is called the external world.

Just as you would demonstrate the power of a banyan seed that has grown into a tree with vastly spreading branches, O Supreme Śiva, so too [do you manifest] the seed of eternal truth and consciousness within the field of will, endowed with the family of the senses of superior intellect, through your own activities in every respect.
When you manifest your own self in its universal form, then you shall become an object of perception.

(12) Apart from the activity of his own entire sensory faculty, where are the five elements? Where is the manifold world of perception? Where are the sounds and such, and where are the sentences and so forth?

Engaged through these very [faculties] as its own domain, it unfolds as the soul of the entire universe; therefore, you are the foremost of the world—the non-dual, devoid [of distinctions], and the self-luminous object of knowledge. || 5 ||
O Giriśa, the three states of time, the ten directions, the earth sevenfold, water, fire, wind, and the all-pervading ether as the eleventh sense—
these are the infinite seeds of diverse meanings, whose greatness is manifested by infinite consciousness.
O Lord, those born from seeds attached to you surely follow your own quality because of their nature.
The garland of fifty letters, which manifests the network of reality through the utterance of various sounds, is the very nature of the knowledge transmitted from the mouth of the Guru of Giriśa;
it is the science of the manifold and diverse Siddhāntas that issued from the mouths of the Vedas prior to the creation of Brahmā and the other gods.
Then, through various languages and modes of expression, she herself reveals to you the Vedas along with their auxiliary branches.
From phonemes arise the elements (dhātus); from them comes the accumulation of various words; from that, the sentence;

from that, the means of valid cognition (pramāṇa) consisting of various conclusions; and from that, the web of established tenets (siddhānta). Thus, that which reveals the manifold nature of reality is Your science of truth (tattvavidyā).
If you alone are the peerless Great Lord, whose nature is the great consciousness that is devoid of succession; || 8 ||

The entire cremation ground is the sacrificial site; the house is the radiant seat of Oṃkāra, the vast place of departure where the Bhairavas, along with the lords of serpents and the Gaṇapas, have appeared mounted upon the wish-fulfilling trees and are gathered there with divine vessels of *arghya*.
O Supreme Śiva, you pervade with your own self the entire universe, fashioned from fire, the sun, and the moon.

The worship of consciousness consists of vision and action; it is the form of Mahārudra as taught by the Guru, wherein the oblations of sense-objects are offered by one's own limb-deities from all sides, while remaining free of conceptual construction.

O Lord, you are offered as an oblation into the fire of the Self by those who are free from desire, who seek only the Self, who have accumulated sacrifices, who are conscious and independent, who are unwearied, and whose intellects have been transformed by the knowledge of Brahman.

Wherein duality is the sinless fuel, the sacrificial animal is the fleshless [pure] consciousness, death is the protection, the tongue is the oblation, and awakening is the manifest fire; the stainless Self alone is the Hotṛ priest, the pure mind is the Adhvaryu, and the group of Mothers known from the mouth of the Guru is the Udgātṛ.
You are my own teacher, the supreme lord of guides; you are the highest Śambhu, the Lord, who is most dear to Umā. || 11 ||
And other sacrifices performed here with sacrificial animals by those possessing desires, which accomplish all established doctrines;
and various sacrificial rites that spread like variegated works within the abode of the three worlds;
and the procedures for the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the universe, whose seeds are the powers of their own actions.
Having arisen from all sides, you manifest through the mind, O you whose form is the creation of wonders! 12.
Thus ends the fifth chapter, concerning the rays of the branch of the power of action (*kriyāśakti*), in the *Paraśambhumahimnastava* composed by the venerable Dūrvāsas. || 5 ||

The Sixth Chapter: The one whose self-power is eternally undiminished, who is inflamed by the fifteenth hood of all the lunar days (tithis), who swallows the winds of time such as the *truṭi* and others with his wide tongue, and who dwells within the anthill of the wheel [of existence].

You are the Lord of the Kundalinī, whose rays are understood through the threads of perfect consciousness; you are the sole master of the universe’s unfolding, the source of the sun, moon, and fire within the path of Kṛṣṇa, and the one whose body is the lord of serpents. || 1 ||

O you whose form is the primordial *suṣumnā*, you experience the supreme [state], in which the power of the substrate (*ādhāra-śakti*) has been awakened by the fires of the lamps within the body through their unimpeded movements; which consists of various great sounds arising from the distinctions of the respective *cakras*; and which is a flowing stream of infinite Brahman-bliss.
Because the *prāṇa* rises upward while the *apāna* rushes downward, therefore, through their non-opposition and by the mere restraint of the wind that generates both,
there occurs the unfolding of the ocean of the equilibrium of flavors (*samarasa*)— the expansion of the dyads of knowledge and ignorance, and so forth— free from all pretension.
Together with that [light], the swan indeed attains dissolution in the supreme splendor; such is your life-thread.
That which produces the illumination of each respective object for all the sense organs;
that from which arise all essences in all actions—such as incomparable objects, fear, joy, and anger;
and from which are born all states of being pervaded by the winds moving through the paths of all the channels.
And you alone are that great vibration which takes various forms and is the path for all migrations.

Having understood through the words of a true guide the divine mudrā known as Khecarī, whose power is well-known, and having restrained within the mind of one's own self the sense organs that are accompanied by the manifold expansion of objects;

O Śambhu, that yogi who contemplates that mind as the limb of light, which is without limit or support, becomes extinguished; having attained Your great vibration, he becomes the path of black [smoke]. || 5 ||
O Lord, this entire world is animated by you through that which is called *prāṇa*, the *kuṇḍalinī*;
knowing her, yogis go to that supreme, fearless, and peaceful state. Without knowing her, they remain bound by cruel karma in the ocean of existence, subject to birth and death.
If she, who is devoid of beginning and end, takes pity, she may release those who are drowning from the bondage of death.
Thus ends the sixth chapter, concerning the mass of rays from the neck of the Kuṇḍalinī-śakti, in the *Paraśambhumahimnastava* composed by the venerable Dūrvāsas. 6.
In this seventh chapter,

having attained the status of the Great Mother known as the eternal and imperishable *svanityākṣara*, he seeks to manifest the self-luminous Brahman-reality that had been hidden within the cave of his own heart.

O Śrī Guru, you, whose majesty is well-known through the knowledge of the divine tradition and who radiate infinite power, teach the state that is your own essential nature by means of the various distinctions consisting of the respective phonemes. || 1 ||
O embodiment of the glorious Word-Brahman, through various sounds and the manifold distinctions of the unstruck resonance (*anāhata-dhvāna*) consisting of all sounds—
residing within yourself as imperishable syllables— by means of many kinds of musical notes and diverse types of instruments,

such as the great drums (*bherī*), kettledrums (*niḥsāṇa*), bells (*ghaṇṭā*), tabors (*dardara*), clay drums (*muraja*), great horns (*mahāśṛṅga*), flutes (*nāla*), and the great rhythmic beats (*tāla*).
O knower of sounds, you speak through your horns, your limbs, and your body, which are like masses of clouds.
You are the cause of the manifestation of the principles (*tattvas*), present in every lunar day; you possess the limbs of the seven cities and the eightfold [empowerments];
you take the form of the union of male and female; your feet are the sun, the moon, and the great fire; you are sixfold in nature;
you have made manifest your power through the consciousness of all intentions; you are the Great Tradition (*mahāmnāya*) and the Vidyā.
The Puruṣa has the nature of the essence and the expansion; therefore, he is the letter 'A', the self of the imperishable (akṣara). || 3 ||

The one primordial syllable (akṣara), consisting of eighteen aspects through its variations of the pleasant, acute, grave, and circumflex accents, abiding in high, low, and both pitches, possessing its own exalted and great manifestation,
and arising as the seven musical notes of the resonant song expanded by the intervals born from the scales beginning with Ṣaḍja—
O You whose nature is the eternal sound, You dwell within various passionate compositions.

(17) You, whose every aspect, station, and color have been first calculated, are praised as the "Sixteenth" (Ṣoḍaśī), manifesting through the power of Your own will the established firmness and the great maturity of Your own majesty.

O you whose essence is the glorious great phoneme (Mahāvarṇa), you— time made manifest, possessing the three genders, and being the very self of both knowledge and ignorance— produce everywhere the dissolution of the world through short, long, protracted, and other [vowel] measures.
O You who are the sole creator of the two wings [of the universe], whose forms are earth, water, fire, air, and ether;
You who have reached all the senses, such as hearing, yet remain bound by Your own nature;
You who abide within as the universal form—the Puruṣa—since You are known through Your own sequence.
O Paramaśiva, you are known by people as the knower of the syllables of the groups; therefore, you are born from the groups.
The mantra-sciences, which reveal the state that is the abode of fire and wind— the dwelling place of the Self transcending all—
shine forth from the lotus-like mouth of the Guru Śiva through an intellect whose intention is fixed on truth; likewise,
the verbal roots with their manifold meanings and the Vedas of the wondrous Word, whose majesty is made manifest.
O Supreme Śiva, everything perishes without you—the innate form consisting of the union of phonemes.

Having gone to the syllable Oṃ, which dwells in one's own self and is praised by the Vedas; having reached the seed-syllable of Speech (Vāgbhava), the seed of Power (Śakti), the seed of Māyā, the seed of Smara, the seed-syllable of the Supreme Splendor, and the pair of seed-syllables of the Mother (Mātṛkā);
and having also reached the end of Śiva and pierced the six peaks shining in the six paths (ṣaḍayana).
I am that Swan, and you are likewise; O you whose form is the mantra, you cease [from activity] within the mind.
By means of the *nyāsa*s—consisting of the *bindu*, *nāda*, and *ūrdhvanāda* together with the pervasive *kalā*s associated with their presiding deities;

by various presiding deities beginning with Ananta who are easily attained through transformation; and by the specific *vidyā*s found in the scriptures spoken by the venerable Guru, as well as the mantras of the various and manifold established doctrines originating from the mouth of Śruti.
With your face spread in all directions, you burn away worldly existence and sin in the fire of the mantra of difficult-to-attain splendor.

The phonemes, the mantra-sciences, the ten transformative operations, the elements, eternal words, sentences, the various divisions of the Vedas, the many kinds of philosophical systems, the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs, and the spoken languages; the various meters, musical rhythms, and the qualities of the modifications of tone— all these are situated within the realm of speech.
Various forms were born from that supreme fire, from the seed-syllable of the power of the Mother (Mātṛkā-śakti).
Thus ends the seventh chapter, concerning the rays of the Mātṛkā-Śakti, in the *Paraśambhumahimnastava* composed by the venerable Dūrvāsas. || 7 ||
The eighth chapter:
Thus, those very ghaṭikās of Paraśiva existing day and night have become rays;
they take the form of couples of male and female, consisting of the sun and moon, and are red and white as they are traversed by their feet.

The sixfold divisions of the portions of the six powers, situated within the six corners of the pair of small cities, manifest the temporal states through the four ages, which are the causes of all beings.
The thirty-six-fold garland of principles, beginning with the earth and ending with Śiva, whose self-functioning has been attained;

the twenty-seven lunar mansions and their transformations in the ether and the wind; the individual soul, Māyā, and Śiva’s portion; and the transformations of the internal body situated within the fire, such as bone, flesh, and so forth.
Upon the earth, you, like the garlanded one (the sun), illuminate on all sides the multitude of qualities of the illusory power of life.
All those rays of yours, situated in the seats of earth, water, fire, touch, space, and mind, are sixfold in measure and are all indeed Bhairavas of supreme radiance;
yet among them, you alone are the fierce one, manifesting a most transcendent majesty.
O Bhairava-fire of consciousness, you shine all around like the sun situated in the midst of its rays. || 3 ||
O Śiva, the Bhairavīs—the goddesses of your rays—have eyes filled with compassion;
they are gracious, their own worlds having arisen from the channel of the ether of your existence, and they have consumed the task of their own purpose.
They are peaceful within that very abode, [releasing] gods, sages, and ancestors who were bound by merit and sin.
And they swiftly shatter the manifold afflictions of their devotees through the expansion of the fire of self-knowledge. || 4 ||
O Śrīnātha, O Śrīpareśeśvara, O Paraśiva, those divine and most divine rays of yours—
which are established in various wonderful and manifold forms that are inaccessible to the mind and speech of Brahmā and the other gods— [shine forth].

How indeed could any mortal poet be capable of praising or knowing You, whose secrets are profound and manifest, and who remain uncomprehended even by the words of gods and sages? What insignificant human here is not dull-witted [in this task]? || 5 ||
Thus ends the eighth chapter, the Section on the Analysis of the Rays of the Sixfold Lineage, in the *Śrī-Dūrvāsakṛta-Paraśambhu-Mahimnastava*. 8.
The ninth section: Gaṅgā is his chariot, Śatāṅga (the hundred-limbed) is the earth, Śatadhṛti (the hundred-sustainer) is its charioteer, the seven horses are the Vedas,
the two Puṣpavantau (sun and moon) are his wide-spreading wheels, and Brahmā is the axle known by the one Veda.
The remainder is the binding of its rope; above that is the realm of the ancestors (Pitṛloka), where you should contemplate yourself as the charioteer. || 1 ||
To the one who possesses the splendor of infinite suns at the end of an eon, who has many formidable fangs and six faces,
who is surrounded on all sides by fire, moon, sun, water, and the eight directions,
blazing with rays of light; who holds a trident, sword, arrow, fierce spear, goad, excellent human head, and *bilva* fruit as weapons, and whose enemies are seated upon his feet—
I praise you, the Guru Śambhu, who holds in the circle of your own arms the radiant noose and the gesture of fearlessness. || 2 ||
With great earrings as ornaments reaching to his ears, fashioned from the moon-like bones of serpents,
his body encircled by a garland of skulls that resounds in all directions,
and his waist-band constructed from the vast hides of intoxicated lordly elephants, he laughs with a loud, boisterous laugh.
I take refuge in Him, who is the size of a thumb held within the cavity of the radiant sky of the heart. || 3 ||
In the cremation ground, he is surrounded on all sides by lords of the nāgas, kalpavṛkṣa trees, birds, terrifying gods and demons, bhūtas, pretas, and piśācas, as well as yoginīs;
he is the sole abode of all wisdom, the refuge of the three worlds, and is illuminated within himself through the supreme self.
I praise you, the Guru Śambhu, whose face is fire, the Lord of the reality of the Self that transcends all. || 4 ||

He whose grace consists of the perfected form of Śiva-nature manifested through the yoga of various meditations, and who has dispelled the intense delusion of the three [guṇas] by splitting them with the triple-pointed [weapon] consisting of will, knowledge, and action; (p. 22)

O All-pervading Supreme Śiva, you are the one whose enemies—the false cognitions—are pierced by the sword of true knowledge; you are the target for those whose ignorance has been severed by the blade of their own yoga; therefore, you are the Conqueror of Death. || 5 ||

O Lord, Your triple power (*triśakti*)—which destroys the very time of the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe—is that Māyā-power; she is the fierce, haughty, and massive elephant, while that [power] is the goad (*sṛṇi*) that restrains her.
Furthermore, these [powers] are Your excellent gifts, skillful in bestowing virtue, wealth, the self, desired objects, and liberation.
You are the one who shatters the terrifying and fierce Death that devours all; therefore, You are the Death of Death.
Your noose, which brings all under control, was fashioned by the Lord of the Ancestors; your elephant has the gait of a lion; your discus is the rising sun for the night of saṃsāra;
and your Pināka bow is your supreme Self, seated upon the Great Mother (Mahāmātṛkā) who consists of the entire nature and its transformations, having overcome all delusion.
O Lord, your vital breaths are that skull, which has the form of the consciousness of a deceased spirit whose mouth is directed toward the face of the Destroyer.
Thus is your supreme majesty, possessed of divine and celestial weapons, sung by the Vedas and Shastras;
you were previously described as having a hundred limbs, and yet you move from the head of the host of ancestors upon the stage.
Your fierce Tandava dance causes fear to the three worlds, and your loud laughter is like the falling of a thunderbolt.
Out of fear of you, as of no other, there is nothing else that is superior; therefore, you are the fierce hero.

Seated upon the throne of the mind, ether, wind, fire, water, earth, and the Lord of the Dead (Śiva), his form manifested through the six powers, he is the traveler on the path of the six entrances; his feet are the Moon, the Sun, and Fire;
he is the Fire of Brahmā, who has devoured with his seven tongues the entire phenomenal world that had become an object of experience.
Though you are gross, you are inaccessible even to the light of those whose vision is meditation and who are most free from darkness.
(23) Thus,
although he is to be contemplated through the meditation described above, his nature remains uncomprehended by the activities of mind and speech;
he is the self-willed one whose own existence is consciousness, whose power is appropriate to that consciousness, the purifier, whose form is Śambhu.

O Maheśa, he whose inner being dwells within that Reality—even though its nature transcends all things—when investigated through the knowledge proclaimed in the Upaniṣads, shall become identical with You, Śiva. 10.

Though glorious, he is the first mendicant; though the progenitor of the three worlds, he is self-born; though knowable through the explanations of scriptural utterances, he is beyond words; though naturally pure, he sports with his own *māyā*;
though one in essence, he is manifold; though devoted to the supreme maiden, he is the knower of the Self who is served by all.
Therefore, you, whose conduct is spontaneous, triumph here over the mental fluctuations of emotion.
Thus ends the ninth chapter, on the yoga of meditation upon the Purifier (Fire), within the *Paraśambhumahimnastava* composed by the venerable Dūrvāsas. || 9 ||
The tenth chapter:
You are to be seen by the worlds through manifold methods and the words of all established doctrines;
you are to be heard as the non-conceptual Śiva from the lotus-like mouth of the awakened Guru.

He whose feet are graced by all principles must be meditated upon; He who rests upon that [foundation] and relies solely on pure existence—there is no god other than You, O Immortal One, whose feet are praised by the gods. || 1 ||

I bow with manifold hymns of praise to the fierce and peaceful hero, the Great Viṣṇu who consists of all things, the blazing fire whose infinite faces are everywhere, who possesses the body of a man-lion, the terrifying one who is auspicious to all,
the omniscient one who is the death of Death, and who is worshipped by all the worlds.
I worship you, O Guru, the King of Mantras, the Supreme Śiva who has manifested as the universal ego. 2.
O Śambhu, you whose body consists of the worlds Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, Tapaḥ, and Satya;
you whose power is woven by the Vedas and the Brahmins, as well as by the Antarikṣa, Dyau, Sūrya, Candra, Ācārya, Indu, Śukra, and Arkī;
you who, through the divisions of Prāṇa, Apāna, and the rest, cause the entire mental yoga of meditation to manifest.
For those who possess that worship, there arises the state of being a Brahmā created by the gods and the state of being a yogin.
We meditate upon that most excellent, supreme, incomparable, and desirable *bhargas* of the divine Savitṛ, which the sages declare to be our "wisdom" (*dhīḥ*)—
the Aurva-fire, the fourth state, attained by all beings, stainless, and the primordial source of vision and action in every respect.
O glorious Maheśa, I meditate upon the object of meditation, just as it is meditated upon by yogis whose internal organs are perfectly restrained.

O Śiva, time is infinite, consisting of the ages (yugas), days, nights, fortnights, months, and likewise years; its divisions are the six seasons, which comprise all the various occurrences of the world that follow them.
The performers of various sacrifices, the gods, the sons of Diti, humans, all the nāgas,
the lords of yogins, and the multitudes of living beings enter the cavity of your feet from the midst of their births until the end of existence.

In the abode of the three worlds, you wander pervading all that has been, that is, and that will be, endowed with the six great powers and joined with the desires for creation, maintenance, and destruction;
[you move] among gods, demons, humans, the hosts of serpent-lords, and the expansion of all living beings.
O Śiva, with your limbs adorned by your own [powers], you are the sun beyond the darkness of worldly existence. || 6 ||
He is the hearer, the toucher, one who relishes his own essence, the knower within all fragrances,
the speaker, the doer, the goer, the creator of the universe, and the one who delights in the three worlds;
he is the lover, the investigator, and the one whose fame has purified the world pervaded by his seven crests of flame.
You are the awakener of infinite self-interests, you have attained the practice of all things, and you are Śiva. || 7 ||
He who seeks all goals, who bears all names, the lord of all lineages, the sovereign of the courtyard of all worlds;
he is the erotic, the enjoyer of all pleasures, a connoisseur of the nine rasas, and the ruler of a vast empire;
he is celebrated in the world of speech throughout the three realms as the performer of the Soma sacrifice and the sacrifice itself.
O Śiva, that person who is called by people a worldly wanderer acting according to desire is truly blessed when he [worships] you.

The field, the knower of the field, the deity presiding over the Aghora-mantra from the mouth of the Guru Śiva, the mantra, the deity presiding over the mantra, the stainless ritual procedure of sacrifice, the category of reality fit for yoga—
you are the New Moon, the Full Moon, the enclosing sticks, and the preeminent master of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ priest—
O Śambhu, without you there would be no chanter, no officiating priest, and no oblation for the threefold fire.

All the gods, as well as humans, serpents, and all living beings, are the knowers of the field (*kṣetrajña*); and that field is the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*), pervading the abodes of the three worlds and possessing manifold forms.

Having realized You, O Supreme Śiva— the Fire who pervades all this extent and remains therein as the enjoyer of the entire universe and its devotees— the wise man transcends even Great Death by means of Your six powers.

In you, the Supreme Person, the presiding deity of the aforementioned field, whose nature is infinite, all the Vedas— along with their limbs and sub-limbs, the scriptures, and the sciences of various established doctrines— possessing the majesty attained through them, manifest as the specific laws of destiny taught by the gurus according to the divine tradition.
O Three-eyed One, whose form is the universe, your speech shines forth with its own meanings; who else is superior to you? 11.
The root of which is space itself; its middle trunk is wind, fire, water, and earth; the gods are its branches; the Daityas are its clusters of leaves; human beings are its spreading tendrils;
the Nagas are its flowers; and living beings of manifold forms are its awakening of ripened grain.
O Supreme Śiva, you shine forth as the seed of the all-pervading Nyagrodha tree.
In the form of *māyā*, Time (*kāla*) effects birth and death through its operation upon the limbs of all living beings;
yet in the form of *vidyā*, it is celebrated as the "End-maker of Time" (*kālāntaka*). You alone are that, and no other.
Having realized through the Guru that the very egoity of the body is the End-maker, one transcends *māyā*.
O Śiva, by your grace he remains awake in the awakening of the Self; here he shall become the conqueror of death.
You are the Lord, you are the Guru, you are the treasury of the knowledge and meaning of the tradition born of the supreme state;
you are Śambhu, you are the Supreme Ruler, you are of the highest majesty; you are Parā, you are the Supreme Fire;
you are the Sun, you are the Moon, and you are also the Mother, the Father, and the true friend.
You are my brother, you are my kinsman, you are a treasure-trove of wealth; apart from you, I have no other.

It is the substratum of word and meaning, the progenitor of the three worlds, the reality existing in all directions, abiding throughout the triple world, its state known through the three genders, and that which is to be known solely through the single principle of all principles.
Having manifested that which unfolds as the light of supreme glory residing in an all-inexpressible existence, you reveal your own supreme reality before us through your own colors.
You are the universe, the cause of the universe, the sole agent of all effects despite being devoid of instruments,
transcendent to the universe, and the Lord of the universe— thus have you been ascertained in many ways by those who know the Akṣamālā.
You are one whose own sacrificial oblation has been consumed by the abundant flames of the fire of the awakening to the non-dual Self.
O Śrī Śambhu, O existence of the universe, you bestow the worship of nirvāṇa in the supreme ether.

Thus, he who praises this prosperity— vast throughout the three worlds, whose conduct is a universal marvel, whose power is extolled by the teachings of both internal and external scriptures, which is devoid of beginning, middle, or end,
and which manifests as the manifold varieties of living beings, including gods, asuras, humans, and serpents, in both gentle and fierce forms; [he attains that same prosperity].
O Śambhu, he becomes one who is truly a marvel to the world, [having mastered] the stages of arising, abiding, and cessation. || 17 ||
Thus ends the tenth chapter, on Great Sovereignty, in the *Mahimnastava* composed by Śrī Dūrvāsas;
now begins the eleventh chapter:
"What is worship? Who is the worshipper? What is the Guru of Śiva? What is the rite? And what is the mantra?"
What is the seat? What is the flower? What is the pure water? And what are all these ritual offerings here?

For You, the Self who is beyond dualities, how could all this—which is fashioned as a duality—be for the sake of Your satisfaction? O Maheśa, may those whose three organs [of body, speech, and mind] are purified by the worship of stainless knowledge be gracious.

O Moon-crested Lord, for You who pervade all this entire world throughout the three periods of time by the radiance of Your own existence, who possess eight forms, and whose lofty lion-throne is the minds of all beings— whence could there be an invocation for You here, and where could there be an external seat? Your conduct is everywhere.
Māyā intensely fashions the state of saṃsāra and differentiation for the sake of its own enjoyment. || 2 ||

The fire is the support, the sun is the excellent vessel, and you, the Lord of Power (Śaktīśa), are the leader of the digits of nectar— the full wine to be worshipped there within the assembly of vessels consisting of six components;
for you, the rising [nectar] serves as the water for the feet and the libation through the external sacrificial vessels of the Arghya.
How could you be content, O Supreme Śiva, who recline upon the milk-ocean of pure, stainless knowledge?

For the purpose of bathing the body, those three principal channels— residing within the Yamunā, the Gaṅgā, and the intermediate river— are the streams of the flow of knowledge-bliss, which are the eternal joy of the stainless Śiva-knowledge arising from the orbs of the sun, moon, and fire.
Since you were created from the heart-linga form, how could your bath here be performed with other waters? || 4 ||

The sun that dispels the darkness of the illusion of shame, passion, and the like; the mass of light arising from which destroys the gloom of worldly existence for one adorned with the garments of the directions;
whose body is augmented by the sacrificial threads of wisdom—[to him] even death is but an ointment.
Others are mere false pretenses, like the binding of a great thread and the application of ointment upon your garment. || 5 ||
Non-violence toward all, the calming of the swift movement of the senses, compassion for all beings, peace, truth, awakening, unwavering meditative vision through the instructions of the guru,
constant faith and devotion, renunciation of one's own objects of sense, and freedom from desire.
"O stainless Śiva, these flowers are offered for the sake of worshipping you as the worship of consciousness. (6)
The eight Mothers, beginning with Brāhmī, [worship] with flowers of their own respective domains—the blossoms of the Self alone;
the Yoginīs, who are Śaktis, [worship] with clusters of flowers manifesting their own individual majesty;
and those who contemplate Your state of being [worship] with the great Bhairavas that are Your rays, from which limbs have been taken away...
Remembering you, the Lord of Śrī-Cid-Bhairava, they worship you, the Guru who is Supreme Śiva. || 7 ||
By the incense of the constant practice of great latent impressions (mahāvāsanā) placed within the charcoal of the sixfold sciences (sadvidyā),
by the lamps of awakening consisting of the entire Kula tradition (kulāmnāya) issued from the lotus-face of the Illustrious One,
and by the drinking of the great divine offering (naivedya) accumulated through the various foods and objects of all the senses—
O Supreme Lord, how can You, who are to be propitiated by yogis, be satisfied by the acts of others? 8.
Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "Reflection on the Internal Sacrifice and Ritual Conduct," in the *Paraśambhumahimnastava* composed by the venerable Dūrvāsas. 11.
The Twelfth Chapter:
Knowledge as Various Ornaments—sandalwood trees entwined with the fragrance of musk, camphor, and other perfumes; blossoming flowers; and wondrous garments.
Various fragrant incenses, rolls of betel nut like pieces of areca-nut, diverse kinds of drinks, and various vessels are prepared upon the ground for the worship of you, O Supreme Śiva. || 1 ||

These seven oceans situated within the mandala— moving seas of food— [offer] heaps of divine sacrificial offerings consisting of various kinds of cooked foods, diverse meats, vegetables, and various side-dishes;
as well as foods to be chewed, eaten, sucked, and licked, possessing the taste of the various nectars of the moon.
O Śambhu, they also offer wine, curd, clarified butter, and milk as oblations for You. || 2 ||
With lamps in the form of mantras, with various illuminations such as fire, sound, the moon, the sun, the garland of stars, lightning, rubies, pearls, silver, gold, and other minerals—
arranging these for the *nīrājana* rite of You, whose form is self-luminous and primordial— I offer this homage.
The submarine fire illuminates the Supreme Śiva Guru, whose essential nature is the bliss of all.
The mudrās that nourish various meanings, those who have not strayed from the path, the eight yogas, dance,
the treading upon sacred sites, prostration, the movement of one's own organs, the words of all established doctrines,
the currents of action and ignorance, the fan, the great whisks, and the parasol.
Having ascended those elephants, horses, and chariots, he performs service at the feet of the Supreme Śiva. || 4 ||
The sky [is filled] with various sounds: the deep rumblings of clouds at the time of dissolution like the thundering of a great bolt,
the sounds of kettledrums and war-drums, the roar of crashing mountain peaks, and the resonant ringing of many bells.

O All-pervading Lord, here she performs worship with cymbals, sounds, mṛdaṅgas, murajas, and ḍamarukas, with songs and excellent lutes, and with the sounds of all varieties of musical instruments. || 5 ||

The rays of Śambhu are goddesses who have attained the state of supreme equanimity, whose forms are the letters of the Mātṛkā; the eight Bhairavas, radiant and intoxicated by the drinking of the nectar of aesthetic flavor, abide in the Krama sequence.
They proclaim through the Vedāntas and the culminations of the Āgamas that supreme Śāmbhava majesty.
O Lord, O All-pervading One whose form is the universe, you are the state arisen from the ether of an existence that is entirely ineffable.
The Yoginīs and Kṣetrapālas, whose mouths are intent on explaining and meditating upon the true meaning of the Vedas and Śāstras, intoxicated by the honey of the lake;
and the Bhairavas dwelling in the trees of the ten directions of the cremation ground,
heedless from tasting the nectar of the celestial palaces, uttering the loud lion-like laughter of their manifest and formidable arrogance.
O All-pervading Lord, they worship you, the Guru who is Supreme Śiva, with the flowers that are their respective activities. || 7 ||

The *bhūtas*, *pretas*, and *piśācas*, having assumed loathsome forms through the power of their own transformations, and those *yoginīs* who have reached the great deities situated in the enclosure of the cremation ground, illuminate [the scene].
Those gods, the former deities, filled with sweet joy, have their minds overcome by wonder.
Peaceful, they meditate and even sing; O Supreme Śiva, they worship you with joy.
Brahmā with Vedic chants, Hari with lotuses, the fierce Rudra with *tāṇḍava* dances, Mahendra with the threefold arts (*saṃgīta*), the other world-guarding deities with their respective domains,
all the Siddhas and great sages with words of praise and hymns, and all the Durgās and Gaṇeśas likewise [worship].
O Mahādeva Śambhu, they bring forth great joy for you with dances and various kinds of musical instruments.
p.
32) The Śāmbhava fire, searing hot, established upon the lion-throne of the preta,
possesses the fierce splendor of the supreme Ghorā-vidyā, known through its fifty sparks that are the phonemes.

The Lord of Sacrifice, whose rays are satisfied by the oblation of the three worlds through the internal truth, shines here pervading all things with a body manifested from the union of word and meaning. 10.

Like the sun, she swallows with the pride of her profundity the light of wisdom from her own radiance— the wisdom that is the sole ground of all knowledge, the void charnel ground known as Karavīra of the three worlds, the flood of the shoreless ocean of gnosis, and the torrential downpour of understanding from the many scriptures issuing from the mouth of sacred learning.
Your fire, possessing an exceedingly intense radiance, [consumes] the floods of darkness, [rendering] others such as the moon, the stars, and the like insignificant. || 11 ||
O Śrī Śambhu, whose form is the universe, O Supreme Śiva, Guru, Lord, and Soul of the Lord of the Universe—
this worship composed of a garland of verses in the Sragdharā meter, consisting of words meaningful in every respect,
is offered by me; may it be cast into the sacrificial fire of the flame of knowledge within You alone for my liberation.
May my transgression be forgiven; O Lord, recited in the sacred teachings, be gracious to me. 12.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter, the Section on Peace, within the *Viśeṣopacāraparāmarśa* (Reflection on Special Offerings) of the *Śrīdūrvāsakṛtaparaśambhumahimnastava* (The Praise of the Greatness of the Supreme Śambhu composed by Śrī Dūrvāsas). || 12 ||
The thirteenth chapter:
Thus, your worship— which milks compassion and flows with the nectar of sublime devotion— is most effective in dispelling the various manifestations of birth and death.
It generates joy that flows like a river of the bliss of Brahman; it burns away misfortunes, merit, and sin, as well as the forest of this wretched worldly existence. || 1 ||
O Supreme Śiva, my birth is blessed because I have been liberated by the hymn of Your greatness;
for this entire lineage has been split into two parts.
By your grace, they have indeed attained the supreme state. || 2 ||
The death of illusion has been slain by the sword of my guru’s word; the impurity of the mind has been shattered and the darkness of egoism destroyed.
My powerful enemies—desire and the rest—whose domain is the self, have been killed.
O Maheśa, by the brilliance of the fire of excellent discernment known through service to you... [3]
Birth, shame, pride in one's own lineage, the anxiety of all doubts, mental anguish, the egoism of bodily identity, the bond of the duality of merit and demerit, and arrogance—
all these have indeed been destroyed for me by the sun of your great saying.
O Lord, what else could I desire for my welfare than these masses of light? || 4 ||
(34) My practice of this science has become meaningful right here, through your presence and through the scope of your spoken word;
for today you are unassailable, unattainable by the speech or mind of the three worlds, O you whose form is accessible only through every path! (5)
O Lord, having set out upon the path where Śruti and Smṛti meet, I have come entirely under the supreme command of You, the auspicious Guru who is exalted throughout the three worlds;
I worship the Supreme Fire, the consumer of the oblation that is the self of the three worlds.
You are the presiding deity in the forest of worldly existence, blazing forth from yourself.

The state of Brahmā, the leadership of the gods, complete sovereignty over the earth, radiant Brahminhood, the status of a god, yakṣa, nāga, or ancestor, as well as the state of a gandharva or a siddha—
all this is reckoned as utterly impermanent; I do not desire such pleasure.
Nevertheless, O Lord, I desire nothing other than unwavering meditation upon the lotus of your feet. || 7 ||

The fulfillment of purpose has been attained, and the fruitfulness of your speech has reached its goal; by reaching your state, death itself has surely become subject to you. The boundless and fierce ocean of saṃsāra has been crossed, and delusion has been destroyed.
O Lord, merit and sin have both gone to destruction for me; awakening has been attained by me here.
Thus, O Supreme Śiva,
O Śambhu, this hymn of praise to Your majesty has been composed by me through the power of my own speech; may it bring You joy, and may You abide within my heart.
Sever the suffering inherent in existence; practice renunciation and be patient. || 9 ||
As long as this world of living beings— numbering eighty-four lakhs of *paraśiva*-thieves—
undergoes birth and death through the various distinctions of their respective karmas within the terrible wheel of saṃsāra,
it remains subject to the processes of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, being devoid of meditation upon Your boundless feet.
Seeing him utterly terrified and having come for refuge, [he said]: "O God, protect me from death! (10)
Durvāsas, Satyavāsas, Kanakagiri, and I myself reside in the cave known as my heart;
these verses are lions whose claws, paws, and fangs are the weapons of Śiva, possessing singular power,
capable of crushing the herds of fear born from the darkness of illusion, and dwelling in the forest of the knowledge of Brahman.
They lead the speakers, the listeners, and the knowers to the reality of Brahman within the cave of their own hearts. || 11 ||

Having attained on earth an adornment of scholarship that takes the form of the rising rays of the sun, a splendor of appearance, wisdom, great honor, and the difficult path of yoga held in his own hands; having attained longevity, nourishment through Brahman, and fame as pure as Mount Kailāsa; ||| [he shines].
At the end of the body, the wise one, having reached the further shore of Brahman which has the form of the feet of Supreme Śiva, [attains liberation].

Those Brāhmaṇas whose intellects are fixed upon the illustrious Śiva’s teaching, who are diligent in the illustrious [Śaiva] doctrine, whose minds are unclouded regarding the rites prescribed by the Vedas and Smṛtis, who are devoted to truth,
and who are learned in all the Āgamas and in the arts and sciences— they are the true Śāmbhavas.
They attain the state of Brahman by reciting this hymn of praise to the majesty of Śambhu. || 13 ||
Whoever recites this hymn— having received initiation into the Aghora-vidyā from the mouth of a Śiva-guru—

shall, through the light of true knowledge, pierce the powerful enemy that is worldly existence, as well as ignorance consisting of merit, demerit, and the like; thus liberated from conceptual constructs, he attains the bliss honored throughout the three worlds, which is the awakening of the Self.
The hero of hymns attains splendor, fame, fortune, and his desired goal. || 14 ||
He who is devoted to the recitation of the *Mahimnaḥstotra* of the Teacher of the Three Worlds knows the reality of the Supreme Power, the state of Supreme Śiva; he is a wise man.
One who attains the unfathomable depth of praise arising from infinite realization experiences all perfections and shall proceed to the supreme state. || 15 ||

Whoever recites this hymn of great majesty, composed by Durvāsas under the divine name of the venerable Śrī Krodhabhaṭṭāraka, attains lordship over the worlds, eternal preeminence, and the state of Śiva. (16)
There is no god other than Maheśa; there is no hymn of praise greater than Mahiman;
there is no mantra other than Aghora; and there is no reality higher than that of the Guru. (17)
Victorious is the Blessed One, Durvāsas, the foremost teacher of all the Upaniṣads, whose ascetic form assumes both favor and restraint toward the virtuous and the wicked. 18.

May he who is the object of the compassionate grace of the venerable Guru, who is intent upon favoring those who know the Self, and whose awakening consists in the praise of Supreme Śambhu, always remain steadfast as the support of the world. (19)
O Supreme Śambhu, one who recites your hymn on the Sun at the three periods of the day becomes,
through his ingenuity, a teacher of the world who illuminates the universe like the sun.
Therefore, the Great God, who possesses memory, intelligence, awakening, and wisdom, and who knows the Self,
shall compassionately reveal the heart of the Supreme Śambhu to worthy recipients.
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, the Section on Conclusion, in the *Paraśambhumahimnastava* composed by Śrī Dūrvāsas.
Herein concludes the *Paraśambhumahimnastava*, composed by the lord of sages, the highly exalted Dūrvāsas, who is also known by the name of the venerable Krodhabhaṭṭāraka.
